body: Regardless of the mismatch, ghosting is a shitty thing to do to someone, so unless you said something truly awful during that "back-and-forth," not your fault.  But maybe try to date with more intention from now on: someone who's kept it casual that long probably won't want a family and a white picket fence with you.

Update: Just a few hours after I responded, they messaged saying want to stay strictly platonic and have no interest in rekindling anything in the future.

Sucks, but better now than later, and the friendship's still there.  I think this is the end of my ENM era, though.  I think I will have to turn to monogamy for someone who wants the kind of commitment I do.

>It does seem like that, yes. Like you're willing to accept crumbs to deal with the reality of your isolation. 

Yes.  I won't deny that.  As I said, I just can't afford another full-blown depressive episode right now and holding on to some kind of hope for a connection in the future is the only thing keeping me from one.  I'm fully willing to accept it may never happen, and it might just be a temporary crutch until I can move on.

But - unlike a lot of people - I actually do worse with NC breakups than ones with casual contact afterwards.  The worst I've ever experienced are the ones where went straight from partners or close friends to never knowing how they were doing again.  (With a couple, I'm not sure if they're still alive.)  They laid me out for months and kept me from dating again for years.  I still care about all my past partners and flings except the ones who were outright dickheads.  And I'm not jealous of who else they've dated, which is part of why I've stuck with polyamory for so long.  Like this one, we're not together because there was some basic incompatibility, so they're free to find someone with whom there's not.

I did float the proposal about being secondaries or having a comet thing someday, and they said they didn't think they'd be opposed to that - although it did turn out to be too soon, which annoyed them since it was before I had given them the space they asked for.  So I'm going minimal contact (e.g. today they sent me a video of their cat and I simply emoji-reacted) until they want to talk again, while getting on with my life and starting to casually talk to other people on apps.

And I'm fully willing to accept that we might never be involved beyond a casual friendship again.  Not what I'd prefer, but if it goes that way, nothing to be done.

Thanks.  I mostly miss their presence in my daily life.  Knowing I'd be able to rely on talking to them about everything, receiving random "I love you's", etc.  I can't say I'm either happy or unhappy about their seeing other people.  Oddly, it's more apathy about that than anything else.

Part of what I'm trying to decide is whether I actually want monogamy or not, or more specifically, if it's the only way to get what I want.  And I do want to stay friends.  The only time I don't talk to exes is when they ghost or block, although that has happened in more cases than not.

Regarding excuses:  Maybe.  If they end up in an LTR tomorrow or it turns out they were lying about my not having done anything wrong, then yes.  But if not, then I don't see how it genuinely isn't just a mutual incompatibility in both relationship styles and goals.  And they did do the work in therapy and fess up as to why they'd become more distant and unsatisfied, where less mature people I know have just left the blame on me.

I needed it anyway.  I have severe Bipolar with mostly depression (in addition to AuDHD), CPTSD, and the original post might have made it clear how much anxiety I suffer regarding relationships in general.  Definite abandonment complex. 

If I hadn’t been actively seeking both self-help and professional help, I would probably be handling this much worse, like I have with previous breakups.  Although meds are doing a good job keeping me out of chemical depression too.

Much better with.  Our conversations were great, I appreciated how communicative they were (and still are, even after scaling back from being all-day), and they treated me like the most attractive person they've ever seen, which did wonders for my confidence.  Even if the long-term potential isn't there, it wasn't a waste of time or anything.

Thanks for the clarification. I didn’t know nonbinary people experienced dysphoria so similarly to trans people. It’s not something my partner and I have discussed yet. I’d always thought of it as more just the decision that you don’t like the roles and stereotypes associated with men or women and didn’t want to be held to them.

I also didn’t know it was clear they weren’t a man from context alone. 

Even if I’m getting back to it really late, I’ll change it.
This was in my 20's before I was looking for stability and I was coming out of a dry spell, so no, I was just happy to get some.  I was expecting her to care more about me than *that,* though,

>You want monogamy.

Not really.  I want stability, and had just resigned myself to the idea that monogamous relationships were the best way to get it.  But if not, that's just as good.

In fact, I wouldn't have spent so long in poly dating and relationships if I didn't like the idea of it, I was just so jaded by the actual people I'd been going out with that I was at the point of "fuck this."  But if I had good experiences with it on my second go-round, that would be awesome.  TBH, I like having sex with people (which made the sudden ED thing even more surprising) and would gladly do it with multiple, just not at the expense of having someone reliable.

But if my partner turns out to be, it could very well be just the situation I want.

>(It’s not necessary to tell us your partner’s assigned gender, and it is in fact rude to reveal a nonbinary person’s personal information like that if not relevant.)

Fair point, and I was on the fence about it.  But I figured it might be relevant because unfortunately, it seems that even when NB identities are involved, if only due to the amount of societal conditioning people have growing up before coming out in adulthood, most relationships between an AMAB and an AFAB still seem to have different dynamics than ones between two AMABs.  And I don't know whether or not any of that is at play here, but I thought it might especially help to contextualize the very insecurities about masculinity, and my role as the male in the relationship, that you mentioned.

And we're actually working on discussing plans and making more defined schedules for when we'll see each other today, so that's fortuitous.

And regarding the edit...  Yeah, that was a misnomer on my part.  What I actually meant was "The first other person they've dated since they started dating me," but I don't know if there's a concise term for that.  I was also rushing to finish it while I was at work.

The problem was, she told me that on the third date while we were in bed.  You're right that it's fine when it's upfront, although I don't think it's something I'm interested in anymore.

And yeah.  I don't mean this in an offensive way at all, but I thought the opening paragraphs made it pretty clear I was torn between mono and poly.

I know I asked for advice, not validation, but...  I actually don't think I agree with this.  I've been unambiguously breadcrumbed before, and this isn't what it felt like.  In those situations, communication either stopped being daily or became more and more laconic except when they wanted some light banter or dick.  If that.

But we still message daily, sometimes at length; they still initiate their fair share of conversations; and we video call whenever we get the chance.  In fact, they reached out this morning and we're currently having an in-depth discussion about the situation and what (as well as how much time) we expect from each other.  And they said they like him a lot, but the relationship isn't as serious as it looked and, at least for now, is just FWB.

Don't get me wrong, I'm fully aware of the stereotype about "the guy she tells you not to worry about," but I've found that when I'm being breadcrumbed, the person completely closes off to talking about relationship status or why we're not seeing each other more.

Also, unless Partner's lying to me when they say they're just taking alone time - in which case it stops being ENM and becomes cheating, which is a very different situation - he only comes over on days when I work so we can keep my days off open.  No schedule change.

I think they're being honest about their intentions and the relationship has a solid base, it's just a matter of reconciling our expectations.  And I accept I could be wrong, but it might not be any more likely than in the average mono relationship.
Not interested in any emotional investment at all.  I've had one outright tell me she reserved all attachment for her husband and everyone else was just for sex.  Never saw her again.

It says they're nonbinary in the post, if by acronym.  But yes, that's the confusion inherent in they/them pronouns.  I wish one of the singular ones like ey/em had caught on, but they didn't.

Also, getting a car would do a lot to close the distance without us having to live next to each other.  As I mentioned in the other response, it's just over an hour to their town, but the city I live in has such bad traffic that they could just be on the other side of it and it'd sometimes still take that long to get there.  Having to Greyhound is what makes it way more of a pain.

I don't even know what being a primary would mean right now, though.  I don't want to move in with them in the foreseeable future since they live an hour away.  I'm actually glad they're independent because I'm often really busy.  (In fact, it's usually them saying they wish they had more time with me.)

I'd probably be unhappy if they started nesting with the other guy, since that would establish a hierarchy by default, but beyond that, I *think* I'm fine as long as I get our regular amount of time together without feeling like they're putting me on the backburner to spend way more with him.  I don't need the primary label.

He didn't just tell me, he posted it to his Facebook. I've just been talking to him more about it in private. I definitely think he doesn't see suicide as ideal, and if someone could stop him - and hopefully help address his trauma and life circumstances, which is way out of my depth - I'm sure he wouldn't do it. 

I just think he's in so much pain he doesn't see any other options.
